reason: e14 plus three timezone splits, round of 2026-11-21 (specs/dsl.md, Time zones; specs/research/tz-taxonomy.md): test_tz_writers (510 rows from two LLM writer sets: voice and non-native English, terse quick-add and chat; two agreeing labelers), test_tz_web (532 rows from web sources held out whole by a hash of the source name: parser tests and standards, announcements and status pages, questions and converters; two agreeing labelers), test_tz_context (104 generated rows that carry a context {zone, locale} and test the choice among ambiguous abbreviations IST, CST, BST, AST, EST, PST; labels come from the policy table, not from an engine). Pool halves for tuning: data/pool/tz/dev_p01 to dev_p08. Rows in the sealed splits that were also in the pool, e14 or earlier web rounds were removed.
known_issues: The collection agents' reports on web rounds 12 to 14 (read before the pool and sealed split) named zone constructions that also occur in sealed sources. This is design-level knowledge, not row-level; the sealed rows were not mined.

tz-w2 (a writer set) was discarded: 197 of its 322 rows copied writer 4's (a sealed set). tz-w6 replaced it. Writer sets share the same families in near-equal proportions because the brief fixed the shares.
test_tz_context labels come from the policy table (specs/tz-zones.md and specs/dsl.md), written by script, not labeled by two labelers and not produced by any engine.

Labels follow specs/dsl.md as of 2026-11-21, including these decisions: the first (time, zone) pair is the label, 'local time' and similar give no zone, a bare place after a time gives no zone, out-of-scope forms are x.
test_tz_web is mostly machine and developer text (ISO timestamps, test-suite strings); web-14's largest source (440 rows, Hacker News search) is capped at 30 rows per source in the labeled data.
